chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Writing "You Showed Me the Way" with Bud Green
summary: Robbins paired McRae's melody with lyricist Bud Green; credit was shared with Ella and Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, there was a song that you composed, or at least, co-composed. "You Showed Me The Way." This was 1937. She recorded that.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Yeah. I did a song -- At that time, I wasn't too good on lyrics. I knew all the top writers, because I was on the Robbins Music staff. It took some doing to get on that staff, because they had all these big writers on that.
A fella named Bud Green was in California at that time. And he just had came back from California.
And Jack Robbins called me one day and says, "Come down, I want to talk to you about that song you brought in the other day."
He say, "What kind of lyrics are these, I'm falling for you like the water off the fall, plaster off the wall," you know. He say, "What kind of lyrics are these?"
I said, "Well, you know."
He say, "Look, not bad.. I have a fella here who just came from California." He said he had -- "didn't do anything out there. Maybe you'll be lucky to him. We're going to give him your song."
I really liked Bud Green. He's a good
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
lyrics writer. Bud came in and he introduced me to Bud. "Okay, you (inaudible), Bud's going to write the lyrics."
You got to remember, Chick Webb and Ella and the whole band, we're all one family. Like this is not just a musician just coming to work, or something.

This band is like a one big family (inaudible). And tell you, being music director -- Like I said before, you have a lot of things -- you got to come up with a lot of ideas. Why you got that job, why do you (inaudible), why you (inaudible). make you straw boss? Why

You have ideas. It's something that you are doing. When I first joined the band, the first night that I played with the band, Charlie Buchanan stuck his head out the door and said, "Who's that tenor player you have," you know. He said, "Maybe that's what Chick needed all the time. A fella that could play all around."
I wasn't that great. I never called myself a great tenor player -- never in my life. I
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
just was a good tenor player. I just played what was supposed to be done. You got a job, you do -- see the situation (inaudible), you do the best you can, you know.
So anyway, Bud Green took the song. And we didn't hear from him for about four weeks -- four or five weeks.
So one day we get another call to bring Ella down and Chick came down -- we all went down to 799 Broadway (inaudible) -- 7th Avenue to Robbins Music.

Two piano players came in, and we all sitting around his office. The fella with the gray hair, (inaudible) concert piano, he played the melody (inaudible). And handed a copy to Ella. So (inaudible) Ella sing. She ran it down -- Ella looked at the lyrics and (inaudible) Ella sing it.
Another piano player got on and played it. You know, jazz piano (inaudible). (Inaudible) big band sound. (Inaudible).
All song pluggers had piano players on their staff that could play any type of song. You know, if you want to demonstrate a song to a band, you know,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
or somebody singing with a band, you want them (inaudible) instrumentally to play that.
Then if they want to play if for a ballad, they bring in a different type of piano player, you wanted (inaudible) classic (inaudible), you know -- things like that.
So anyway, got down to the -- the other fella -- piano player for the band. I think he's from the band from the Pennsylvania Hotel (inaudible). One of these (inaudible).
Jack Robbins had two or three bands that was playing his music -- hotels (inaudible), you know.
So they had like two or three piano players, which was (inaudible) sitting over there. So they played the song for Ella. It was beautiful. Good lyrics so Ella sang it, you know. So that was it.
So now, after everybody had left, there was just Jack Robbins, Bud Green, Ella Fitzgerald and myself.
We were sitting around talking. So she said, 'Teddy, what're you going to do? How many
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
names (unaudible)?"
"Put everybody" --
I put Ella's name on it. She's going to put Chick's name on it and Bud Green. So you see three names on "You Show Me The Way."
Four names, actually.
Yeah, four names.
Bud Green's name is first on the copy that I have.
Yeah. Bud Green did the lyrics, I did the melody, and Ella was just -- they were just cutting on the song.
Well --
We had a habit of doing that. I don't know why, but it's just like a one family thing, you know.
